title: Use a county choropleth for a pattern across thousands of places, and rank none of them.
rule: Shade every county by its class in four sequential steps, with no county lines, the state lines thin and gray, and a county with no estimate unshaded with an edge, named in a note. Set the classes, their note and the words by Rule 14.9’s test for small places, so the map reads as a pattern. Put the national figure above the map (Rule 14.6), group the table by state and give every county with its margin in the download.
use_when: The reader asks how a figure varies across the whole country, place by place, and the pattern matters more than any one county.

use_instead.when: A count, such as jobs, where people or work cluster

text: Counties show the pattern inside the states, such as cities against their rural neighbors. Small counties carry wide margins, so a county map answers “where” in broad strokes and leaves exact figures to the table.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form county-choropleth: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s81; encode id (the geoid, in the layer’s order) and cls (each county’s class, written by a derive script so the page carries one small number a county); table.group groups the table by state, and the CSV export lists every county.
